descriptors.definition: The risk adjusted discount rate technique scales up the required return to compensate for project-specific risks exceeding baseline levels. It combines a risk-free rate reflecting time value and inflation with an investor-driven risk premium.
inclusion: Adding risk premium to the risk-free rate
Upward adjustment of discount rates for high-risk projects
Calculation of net present value using adjusted rates
exclusion: Using unadjusted overall firm cost of capital for high-risk ventures
Qualitative risk assessments lacking numerical discount rate adjustments
nearby_distinctions: Differs from sensitivity analysis by directly modifying the discount rate rather than testing individual variable fluctuations.

descriptors.definition: Sensitivity analysis is a modelling procedure that measures the impact of varying individual project variables on outcomes like net present value or internal rate of return. It helps identify which single factor holds critical significance for the planned project results.
inclusion: Isolating single variables to study outcome effects
Computing net present value changes under adverse percentage variances
Ranking variables by degree of impact
exclusion: Simultaneous multi-variable random shock evaluations without isolation
Adjusting discount rates for inherent project risk
nearby_distinctions: Differs from risk adjusted discount rate by keeping the discount rate constant while testing distinct operational variables.

descriptors.definition: A replacement decision evaluates whether an existing operational asset should be superseded by a new or alternative machine of equivalent functionality. It requires determining the net incremental effect by eliminating cash flows of the old asset and incorporating cash flows of the new asset.
inclusion: Evaluating substitution of existing machinery with newer models
Calculating incremental changes in cash sales and operating expenses
Factoring in salvage value realization of replaced equipment
exclusion: Evaluating entirely new greenfield expansion projects
Investments lacking an existing operational asset base to supplant
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard expansion decisions because cash flows generated by the retired asset must be subtracted from the evaluation.

descriptors.definition: This process details the financial mechanics of substituting an older operating asset with a newer alternative fulfilling identical functions. The evaluation incorporates initial net cash outflows adjusted for tax consequences on book versus market values alongside subsequent operational cash flow changes.
inclusion: Computing tax liability or savings from old equipment disposal
Adjusting new equipment cost by old asset market realization and tax effects
Including depreciation impacts through tax shifts
exclusion: Standalone asset acquisitions without prior equipment displacement
nearby_distinctions: Focuses specifically on step-by-step net cash outflow calculations and tax shields arising from asset exchanges rather than general replacement concepts.

descriptors.definition: The optimum replacement cycle determines the ideal lifespan to retain an asset undergoing decreasing efficiency and rising operating costs. It employs the Equivalent Annual Cost method to render net present values of varying project durations comparable.
inclusion: Computing equivalent annual cost across different retention periods
Selecting replacement periods that minimize annualized outflows
exclusion: Single-horizon capital budgeting without recurring replacement implications
Static asset evaluations ignoring operating cost inflation over time
nearby_distinctions: Differs from single-period replacement decisions by incorporating annualized cost equivalencies to compare multi-year holding choices.

descriptors.definition: The adjusted present value method evaluates capital projects by completely separating investment decisions from financing decisions. It calculates project value by summing the unlevered base case net present value and the present value of tax benefits derived from debt financing.
inclusion: Separating investment and financing cash flow evaluations
Using unlevered cost of equity for base case net present value
Adding present value of interest tax shields to base value
exclusion: Discounting all project cash flows using a single weighted average cost of capital
Combining financing effects directly inside standard discount rate modifications
nearby_distinctions: Unlike standard discounted cash flow methods utilizing weighted average cost of capital, this approach explicitly isolates and adds debt tax shields separately.
